note: Found on 2026-10-02. A Wenner sheet of resistances whose apparent resistivity holds at 9 ohm-m to a = 12 m and halves by 15 m, a drop no layered earth makes. The second layer's resistivity runs to the 0.5 ohm-m bound and no inversion converges: Python reports, unconverged, a fit of 15.26 percent after its 60 iterations, 15.14 after 200 and a three-layer 13.14 after 2000. The browser stops at its own 60 iterations at 15.19 percent with a different boundary (11.14 m against 11.20 m). Each engine reports where its iteration cap left it, so the difference is the cap, not either engine's arithmetic.
open: What should be reported for an inversion that has not converged when max_iterations runs out: the model where it stopped (today, in both engines, with converged = False and nothing in the report saying so), the model with a warning, or a refusal? Until that is decided two engines that take different paths down a slope with no floor stop at different models.
